chunks: 1553 - And Hammad ibn 'Uthman al-Naab narrated from him, عليه السلام, that he said:

“Regarding istikhārah, a man should seek guidance from Allah in the last sajdah of the two rak'ahs of Fajr one hundred and one times, and praise Allah and send blessings upon the Prophet and his family. Then he should seek guidance from Allah fifty times, then praise Allah and send blessings upon the Prophet and his family, صَلَوَاتُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِمْ, and complete the one hundred and one.”

key_terms.الِاسْتِخَارَةِ: seeking divine guidance from Allah regarding a matter
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيِ الْفَجْرِ: the two rak'ahs of Fajr in which this practice is performed
key_terms.سَجْدَةٍ: the prostration in salat where this supplication is to be done
key_terms.يَحْمَدَ اللَّهَ: to praise Allah as part of the etiquette of supplication
key_terms.يَسْتَخِيرَ اللَّهَ: to ask Allah for what is best
key_terms.يُصَلِّيَ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ وَآلِهِ: to send blessings upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and his family

ai.seo_question: How is istikhārah performed in the last sajdah of the two rak'ahs of Fajr according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches a specific manner of istikhārah during the final sajdah of the two rak'ahs of Fajr. It emphasizes repeating the request for divine guidance together with praising Allah and invoking blessings upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and his family, showing the etiquette and devotional structure of this act.
